title: License plate reader and facial recognition bills
summary: Bill 113 would ban selling or commercial use of license plate reader data, and the committee added an amendment barring contracts with certain camera vendors. Bill 112 on facial recognition, a technology police say they do not have, was deferred.

timeline.text: The committee deferred, or put off, Bill 112 with no objections.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A police lieutenant suggested demonstrations and discussion with members before any decision on facial recognition.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Members passed an amendment, eight to zero, so the County must not sign or renew a license plate reader contract with certain vendors.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A police lieutenant said 11 cameras helped solve at least 40 cases in about a year.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Committee staff will send a follow-up letter for the exact yearly camera license costs.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Police said the department owns the camera data and Motorola cannot access it.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A police lieutenant said 27 license plate reader cameras came bundled with 400 radios in a 2025 Motorola contract.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Two bills were on the agenda: Bill 113 on license plate reader data and Bill 112 on facial recognition technology.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Another testifier asked for a 30-day limit on keeping camera data.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The lieutenant said license plate readers record a plate, image, time and location but do not identify people.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A police lieutenant said the police department does not currently have facial recognition technology.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Bill 113 would ban selling or commercial use of automated license plate reader data.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
